args.body:
PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY-CLIENT COMMUNICATION

REDLINE REVIEW MEMORANDUM
Concession Agreement — TxDOT Counterparty Markup

Practice Area: Energy & Natural Resources
Re: Analyze Counterparty Markup of Concession Agreement — Redline Review Memorandum
Output: redline-review-memorandum.docx

Prepared by: Law Firm Company — Energy & Natural Resources practice group
Subject: Reconcile the TxDOT counterparty markup against the base materials, negotiation playbook, disclosure schedules/exhibits, and controlling deal-team instruction, and present a redline review with risk ratings and counter-proposal language.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
I. SCOPE AND PURPOSE
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
This memorandum analyzes the counterparty ("TxDOT") markup of the Concession Agreement against (i) our original draft and the firm's negotiation playbook (the base materials), (ii) the disclosure schedules and exhibits that qualify the base materials (disclosure schedules governing over general statements), and (iii) the controlling deal-team instruction as reflected in the latest partner correspondence. The deliverable reconciles every deviation introduced by the TxDOT markup, assigns a risk rating to each, and sets forth recommended counter-proposal language.

Controlling Instruction. The latest controlling message from deal team leadership provides that the client (i) will concede the indemnification basket conversion (deductible to tipping basket) but (ii) treats any reduction of the survival period for the core representations as a walk-away issue. The deliverable reflects the latest controlling instruction and not any superseded ordering.

Source Materials Reconcider. The base materials comprise the original draft Concession Agreement (representations and warranties, operating covenants, conditions to closing, indemnification, and termination provisions). The disclosures are set forth in Schedules 3.7 and 5.2 and Exhibit B, which control over general statements in the base materials.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
II. DEVIATION INVENTORY (TxDOT Markup)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
The TxDOT markup accepts most firm-standard provisions but introduces three discrete deviations that must be reconciled:

  Deviation 1  — Indemnification cap silently reduced; indemnification basket converted from a deductible to a tipping basket.
  Deviation 2  — Definition of "Material Adverse Effect" (MAE) amended to add carve-outs for regulatory action of exactly the kind at issue in this matter.
  Deviation 3  — New limitation period shortens the survival of the core representations.

Each deviation is evaluated below by reference to the base materials, the disclosure schedules/exhibits, and the controlling instruction, with a risk rating and counter-proposal language.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
III. DEVIATION-BY-DEVIATION ANALYSIS
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

(III.A) DEVIATION 1 — INDENMNIFICATION CAP REDUCTION + BASKET CONVERSION
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
Description. The TxDOT markup (i) silently reduces the indemnification cap from the firm-standard level set in the base draft and (ii) converts the indemnification basket from a deductible to a tipping basket.

Reconciliation Against Base Materials and Schedules.
- The base draft sets the indemnification cap at a level commensurate with the negotiated liability allocation. The markup reduces that cap without any off-setting concession.
- The basket conversion is expressly addressed by the controlling instruction: the client will concede the conversion of the basket from a deductible to a tipping basket.
- Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities. The reduction of the cap, read together with Schedule 5.2, would silently shift recoverability of those retained liabilities back onto the concessionaire/client. The cap reduction therefore interacts adversely with the retained-liability allocation reflected in Schedule 5.2 even if the basket conversion is conceded.

Risk Rating. HIGH (as to the silent cap reduction); LOW (as to the basket conversion, which is conceded).

Recommendation. Concede the basket conversion per the controlling instruction. Reject the silent cap reduction. Propose that the cap remain at the firm-standard base-draft level, and confirm that the conceded basket mechanics do not alter the Schedule 5.2 retained-liability allocation.

Counter-Proposal Language (Section — Indemnification):
"Indemnification Cap. Notwithstanding the basket mechanics agreed by the parties, the aggregate liability of the Concessionaire for all indemnifiable Losses shall not exceed [base-draft cap amount] (the 'Cap'). The Cap is not reduced by virtue of the Tipping Basket conversion and shall operate for the full term of this Agreement. The parties agree that the basket mechanics set forth in this Section do not modify, expand, or otherwise alter the retained-liability allocation set forth on Schedule 5.2, and all liabilities listed on Schedule 5.2 shall remain recoverable to the full extent of the Cap regardless of the basket type."

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
(III.B) DEVIATION 2 — MAE DEFINITION RESTRICTED BY REGULATORY-ACTION CARVE-OUTS
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
Description. The TxDOT markup amends the definition of "Material Adverse Effect" to add carve-outs excluding (or mitigating) changes resulting from regulatory action — of exactly the kind at issue in this matter.

Reconciliation Against Base Materials and Schedules.
- Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries. These inquiries are precisely the "regulatory action" the markup seeks to carve out of the MAE definition.
- The markup's carve-out is not a neutral market-standard qualifier; it is targeted to strip MAE protection for the specific regulatory exposure identified in Schedule 3.7. Because disclosure schedules control over general statements in the base materials, the carve-out must be measured against the disclosed regulatory inquiries and the client's reliance on MAE protection for that exposure.
- The base draft's MAE definition does not contain a carve-out of this scope and reflects the negotiated allocation of regulatory risk.

Risk Rating. HIGH. The proposed carve-out would eliminate MAE protection for precisely the regulatory exposure the client has relied upon, effectively transferring that regulatory risk to the client.

Recommendation. Reject the regulatory-action carve-out in its proposed broad form. Counter with a carve-out that (i) excludes regulatory action that applies generally to all industry participants and does not target the Concessionaire specifically, and (ii) expressly preserves MAE protection for the two pending regulatory inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7.

Counter-Proposal Language (Definitions — "Material Adverse Effect"):
""Material Adverse Effect" means a material adverse change in, or effect on, the business, assets, liabilities, financial condition or results of operations of the Concessionaire as a whole, other than a change or effect arising from (a) changes in general legal, regulatory or economic conditions applicable generally to companies in the same industry, (b) changes in GAAP or applicable law, or (c) actions by any governmental or regulatory authority that apply generally to the industry and do not disproportionately, and are not reasonably expected to disproportionately, affect the Concessionaire relative to other participants in the industry. Notwithstanding the foregoing, a Material Adverse Effect shall be deemed to occur if a change or effect arises from any pending or threatened regulatory inquiry, proceeding, or action specific to the Concessionaire, including but not limited to the two regulatory inquiries identified on Schedule 3.7, and such limitation shall not apply to exclude such inquiry from the definition of Material Adverse Effect."

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
(III.C) DEVIATION 3 — LIMITATION PERIOD SHORTENING SURVIVAL OF CORE REPRESENTATIONS
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
Description. The TxDOT markup introduces a new limitation period that shortens the survival of the core representations beyond that set forth in the base draft.

Reconciliation Against Base Materials and Schedules.
- Exhibit B to the base materials sets forth the survival matrix for the representations. The markup's new limitation period directly contradicts the survival periods reflected in Exhibit B.
- Because Exhibit B (a scheduled exhibit) controls over general statements in the base materials, the survival matrix is the operative baseline. The markup's shortening would materially reduce the client's ability to pursue claims for breaches of the core representations.
- The controlling instruction is unambiguous: any reduction of the survival period for the core representations is a walk-away issue. This is the single most consequential deviation in the markup.

Risk Rating. CRITICAL / WALK-AWAY. Under the controlling instruction, a survival-period reduction for the core representations is a walk-away issue.

Recommendation. Reject the limitation-period change in its entirety. Insist that the survival periods for the core representations remain exactly as set forth in Exhibit B and the base draft. Do not negotiate around this point; the client treats it as deal-critical.

Counter-Proposal Language (Section — Survival):
"The representations and warranties of each party set forth in Sections [3.x] shall survive the Closing until and through the expiration of the applicable survival period set forth in Exhibit B (the 'Survival Periods'), and the parties agree that the Survival Periods set forth in Exhibit B are the operative survival periods for all purposes under this Agreement. No provision of this Agreement shall be construed to shorten, curtail, or otherwise limit the Survival Periods with respect to the core representations. For the avoidance of doubt, the survival provisions of this Agreement are non-negotiable and shall not be reduced by any subsequent amendment of Exhibit B without the express written consent of the Concessionaire."

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
IV. DEVIATION RECONCILIATION SUMMARY AND RISK RATINGS
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
| #  | Deviation                                                    | Risk Rating   | Recommended Action                                        |
|----|--------------------------------------------------------------|---------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|
| 1  | Indemnification cap reduction                                | HIGH          | Reject cap reduction; concede basket conversion           |
|    | + deductible-to-tipping basket conversion                    | LOW           | Concede (per controlling instruction)                     |
| 2  | MAE regulatory-action carve-out                              | HIGH          | Reject broad carve-out; limit to general/full-industry     |
|    |                                                              |               | and preserve Schedule 3.7 protection                       |
| 3  | Limitation period shortening survival for core reps          | CRITICAL/      | Reject in full; walk-away issue per controlling instruction |
|    |                                                              | WALK-AWAY     |                                                           |

Net Position. Two of the three deviations (2 and 3) are adverse and should be rejected with the counter-proposal language above. Deviation 1 is partly conceded (basket conversion) and partly rejected (cap reduction). The overall posture preserves the client's Schedule 3.7 and Schedule 5.2 protections and the Exhibit B survival matrix.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
V. ADDITIONAL CROSS-REFERENCES AND NOTES
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
- Lender and Surety Materials. The transaction includes lender and surety support contemporaneously negotiated around this concession. Any reduction in the indemnification cap (Deviation 1) or extension of MAE carve-outs (Deviation 2) may affect the credit support and surety exposure; those supporting documents should be conformed if the counter-proposals are accepted. If the cap is held at the base-draft level and the MAE carve-out is limited as proposed, the lender and surety positions are preserved.
- Financial Model. The base financial model assumes recoverability to the full indemnification cap and MAE protection for the disclosed regulatory inquiries. The markup's deviations, if accepted, would each have a negative P&L and balance-sheet impact by shifting regulatory and retained-liability risk to the client. The counter-proposal language above is designed to hold the financial-model assumptions intact.
- Schedule confirmation. Where a schedule or exhibit conflicts with a general statement in the base materials, the schedule/exhibit controls (Schedules 3.7 and 5.2; Exhibit B). All counter-proposals above are drafted to be consistent with that hierarchy.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
VI. RECOMMENDED NEXT STEPS
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Transmit the redline review and counter-proposal language to TxDOT, conceding the basket conversion per the controlling instruction.
2. Hold firm on (a) the base-draft indemnification cap and Schedule 5.2 retained-liability allocation and (b) the MAE definition preserving Schedule 3.7 protection.
3. Do not accept any reduction of the survival periods for the core representations — per controlling instruction this is a walk-away issue and requires escalation if TxDOT persists.
4. If agreement is reached, conform the lender and surety letters and update the financial model to reflect the final cap, MAE definition, and survival matrix.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
This memorandum is a privileged and confidential work product prepared in anticipation of litigation and negotiation and reflects the analysis and recommendations of the firm. It is not legal advice to any third party.

PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY-CLIENT COMMUNICATION

REDLINE REVIEW MEMORANDUM
Concession Agreement — TxDOT Counterparty Markup

Practice Area: Energy & Natural Resources
Re: Analyze Counterparty Markup of Concession Agreement — Redline Review Memorandum
Output: redline-review-memorandum.docx

Prepared by: Law Firm Company — Energy & Natural Resources practice group
Subject: Reconcile the TxDOT counterparty markup against the base materials, negotiation playbook, disclosure schedules/exhibits, and controlling deal-team instruction, and present a redline review with risk ratings and counter-proposal language.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
I. SCOPE AND PURPOSE
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
This memorandum analyzes the counterparty ("TxDOT") markup of the Concession Agreement against (i) our original draft and the firm's negotiation playbook (the base materials), (ii) the disclosure schedules and exhibits that qualify the base materials (disclosure schedules governing over general statements), and (iii) the controlling deal-team instruction as reflected in the latest partner correspondence. The deliverable reconciles every deviation introduced by the TxDOT markup, assigns a risk rating to each, and sets forth recommended counter-proposal language.

Controlling Instruction. The latest controlling message from deal team leadership provides that the client (i) will concede the indemnification basket conversion (deductible to tipping basket) but (ii) treats any reduction of the survival period for the core representations as a walk-away issue. The deliverable reflects the latest controlling instruction and not any superseded ordering.

Source Materials. The base materials comprise the original draft Concession Agreement (representations and warranties, operating covenants, conditions to closing, indemnification, and termination provisions). The disclosures are set forth in Schedules 3.7 and 5.2 and Exhibit B, which control over general statements in the base materials.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
II. DEVIATION INVENTORY (TxDOT MARKUP)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
The TxDOT markup accepts most firm-standard provisions but introduces three discrete deviations that must be reconciled:

  Deviation 1  — Indemnification cap silently reduced; indemnification basket converted from a deductible to a tipping basket.
  Deviation 2  — Definition of "Material Adverse Effect" (MAE) amended to add carve-outs for regulatory action of exactly the kind at issue in this matter.
  Deviation 3  — New limitation period shortens the survival of the core representations.

Each deviation is evaluated below by reference to the base materials, the disclosure schedules/exhibits, and the controlling instruction, with a risk rating and counter-proposal language.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
III. DEVIATION-BY-DEVIATION ANALYSIS
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

(III.A) DEVIATION 1 — INDEMNIFICATION CAP REDUCTION + BASKET CONVERSION
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
Description. The TxDOT markup (i) silently reduces the indemnification cap from the firm-standard level set in the base draft and (ii) converts the indemnification basket from a deductible to a tipping basket.

Reconciliation Against Base Materials and Schedules.
- The base draft sets the indemnification cap at a level commensurate with the negotiated liability allocation. The markup reduces that cap without any off-setting concession.
- The basket conversion is expressly addressed by the controlling instruction: the client will concede the conversion of the basket from a deductible to a tipping basket.
- Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities. The reduction of the cap, read together with Schedule 5.2, would silently shift recoverability of those retained liabilities back onto the concessionaire/client. The cap reduction therefore interacts adversely with the retained-liability allocation reflected in Schedule 5.2 even if the basket conversion is conceded.

Risk Rating. HIGH (as to the silent cap reduction); LOW (as to the basket conversion, which is conceded).

Recommendation. Concede the basket conversion per the controlling instruction. Reject the silent cap reduction. Propose that the cap remain at the firm-standard base-draft level, and confirm that the conceded basket mechanics do not alter the Schedule 5.2 retained-liability allocation.

Counter-Proposal Language (Section — Indemnification):
"Indemnification Cap. Notwithstanding the basket mechanics agreed by the parties, the aggregate liability of the Concessionaire for all indemnifiable Losses shall not exceed [base-draft cap amount] (the 'Cap'). The Cap is not reduced by virtue of the Tipping Basket conversion and shall operate for the full term of this Agreement. The parties agree that the basket mechanics set forth in this Section do not modify, expand, or otherwise alter the retained-liability allocation set forth on Schedule 5.2, and all liabilities listed on Schedule 5.2 shall remain recoverable to the full extent of the Cap regardless of the basket type."

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
(III.B) DEVIATION 2 — MAE DEFINITION RESTRICTED BY REGULATORY-ACTION CARVE-OUTS
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
Description. The TxDOT markup amends the definition of "Material Adverse Effect" (MAE) to add carve-outs excluding (or mitigating) changes resulting from regulatory action — of exactly the kind at issue in this matter.

Reconciliation Against Base Materials and Schedules.
- Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries. These inquiries are precisely the "regulatory action" the markup seeks to carve out of the MAE definition.
- The markup's carve-out is not a neutral market-standard qualifier; it is targeted to strip MAE protection for the specific regulatory exposure identified in Schedule 3.7. Because disclosure schedules control over general statements in the base materials, the carve-out must be measured against the disclosed regulatory inquiries and the client's reliance on MAE protection for that exposure.
- The base draft's MAE definition does not contain a carve-out of this scope and reflects the negotiated allocation of regulatory risk.

Risk Rating. HIGH. The proposed carve-out would eliminate MAE protection for precisely the regulatory exposure the client has relied upon, effectively transferring that regulatory risk to the client.

Recommendation. Reject the regulatory-action carve-out in its proposed broad form. Counter with a carve-out that (i) excludes regulatory action that applies generally to all industry participants and does not target the Concessionaire specifically, and (ii) expressly preserves MAE protection for the two pending regulatory inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7.

Counter-Proposal Language (Definitions — "Material Adverse Effect"):
""Material Adverse Effect" means a material adverse change in, or effect on, the business, assets, liabilities, financial condition or results of operations of the Concessionaire as a whole, other than a change or effect arising from (a) changes in general legal, regulatory or economic conditions applicable generally to companies in the same industry, (b) changes in GAAP or applicable law, or (c) actions by any governmental or regulatory authority that apply generally to the industry and do not disproportionately, and are not reasonably expected to disproportionately, affect the Concessionaire relative to other participants in the industry. Notwithstanding the foregoing, a Material Adverse Effect shall be deemed to occur if a change or effect arises from any pending or threatened regulatory inquiry, proceeding, or action specific to the Concessionaire, including but not limited to the two regulatory inquiries identified on Schedule 3.7, and the foregoing exclusions shall not apply so as to exclude such regulatory inquiry from the definition of Material Adverse Effect."

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
(III.C) DEVIATION 3 — LIMITATION PERIOD SHORTENING SURVIVAL OF CORE REPRESENTATIONS
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
Description. The TxDOT markup introduces a new limitation period that shortens the survival of the core representations beyond that set forth in the base draft.

Reconciliation Against Base Materials and Schedules.
- Exhibit B to the base materials sets forth the survival matrix for the representations. The markup's new limitation period directly contradicts the survival periods reflected in Exhibit B.
- Because Exhibit B (a scheduled exhibit) controls over general statements in the base materials, the survival matrix is the operative baseline. The markup's shortening would materially reduce the client's ability to pursue claims for breaches of the core representations.
- The controlling instruction is unambiguous: any reduction of the survival period for the core representations is a walk-away issue. This is the single most consequential deviation in the markup.

Risk Rating. CRITICAL / WALK-AWAY. Under the controlling instruction, a survival-period reduction for the core representations is a walk-away issue.

Recommendation. Reject the limitation-period change in its entirety. Insist that the survival periods for the core representations remain exactly as set forth in Exhibit B and the base draft. Do not negotiate around this point; the client treats it as deal-critical.

Counter-Proposal Language (Section — Survival):
"The representations and warranties of each party set forth in Sections [3.x] shall survive the Closing until and through the expiration of the applicable survival period set forth in Exhibit B (the 'Survival Periods'), and the parties agree that the Survival Periods set forth in Exhibit B are the operative survival periods for all purposes under this Agreement. No provision of this Agreement shall be construed to shorten, curtail, or otherwise limit the Survival Periods with respect to the core representations. For the avoidance of doubt, the survival provisions of this Agreement are non-negotiable and shall not be reduced by any subsequent amendment of Exhibit B without the express written consent of the Concessionaire."

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
IV. DEVIATION RECONCILIATION SUMMARY AND RISK RATINGS
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

|----|---------------------------------------------------------|------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| 1  | Indemnification cap reduction                           | HIGH             | Reject cap reduction; concede basket conversion        |
|    | + deductible-to-tipping basket conversion               | LOW              | Concede (per controlling instruction)                  |
| 2  | MAE regulatory-action carve-out                         | HIGH             | Reject broad carve-out; limit to general/full-industry  |
|    |                                                         |                  | and preserve Schedule 3.7 protection                   |
| 3  | Limitation period shortening survival for core reps     | CRITICAL/        | Reject in full; walk-away issue per controlling        |
|    |                                                         | WALK-AWAY        | instruction                                            |

Net Position. Two of the three deviations (2 and 3) are adverse and should be rejected with the counter-proposal language above. Deviation 1 is partly conceded (basket conversion) and partly rejected (cap reduction). The overall posture preserves the client's Schedule 3.7 and Schedule 5.2 protections and the Exhibit B survival matrix.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
V. ADDITIONAL CROSS-REFERENCES AND NOTES
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
- Lender and Surety Materials. The transaction includes lender and surety support contemporaneously negotiated around this concession. Any reduction in the indemnification cap (Deviation 1) or extension of MAE carve-outs (Deviation 2) may affect the credit support and surety exposure; those supporting documents should be conformed if the counter-proposals are accepted. The markup's deviations, if accepted, would each have a negative P&L and balance-sheet impact by shifting regulatory and retained-liability risk to the client. The counter-proposal language above is designed to hold the financial-model assumptions intact.
- Schedule confirmation. Where a schedule or exhibit conflicts with a general statement in the base materials, the schedule/exhibit controls (Schedules 3.7 and 5.2; Exhibit B). All counter-proposals above are drafted to be consistent with that hierarchy.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Transmit the redline review and counter-proposal language to TxDOT, conceding the basket conversion per the controlling instruction.
2. Hold firm on (a) the base-draft indemnification cap and Schedule 5.2 retained-liability allocation and (b) the MAE definition preserving Schedule 3.7 protection.
